almanac.settings.denied: Only operators can change the server settings.
almanac.settings.unreadable: The server couldn't read those settings, so nothing changed.
almanac.title: Almanac
almanac.look.tooltip: Switch this screen between the House look and a Minecraft-style look. Nothing else changes.
almanac.footer.mode.dark: Dark mode. Click to switch to light mode.
almanac.footer.mode.light: Light mode. Click to switch to dark mode.
almanac.description.empty: Point at a setting to see what it does.
almanac.reset.tooltip: Put this back to its default
almanac.caption.share.temperate: Temperate biomes: share of rain events
almanac.caption.share.cold: Cold biomes: share of rain events
almanac.caption.share.hot: Hot biomes: share of rain events
almanac.note.server_read_only: These settings belong to the server. Ask an operator if you'd like one changed.
almanac.note.server_without_mod: This server doesn't have Almanac, so there are no server settings to show.
almanac.note.restart_needed: These three are built into the seasonal biomes when the server starts, so a change applies after a restart.
almanac.note.far_terrain: Distant Horizons and Voxy draw far land as it was when they last saw it. With LiteLights on the client, that land shows the season's snow instead, from a coarse map of the biomes the server sends to players who have Almanac. Players without Almanac get nothing new.
almanac.note.palette: Seasonal colours come from assets/almanac/palette.json, which resource packs can replace on clients with Almanac. The server uses the copy in the mod for players without it.
almanac.note.permissions: The Seasons, Weather, Snow and Colours pages are the server's settings. Operators (permission level 2 and up) and the host of a singleplayer world can change them here; the server checks the permission and every value, saves config/almanac-server.json and sends the settings to everyone. On the title screen they are the settings your next singleplayer world starts with. The "On this computer" page is yours alone and lives in config/almanac-client.json.
almanac.note.live_changes: Almost everything applies as soon as you press Done: the calendar, the shares of rain, melting, catching up and the copies for players without Almanac.
almanac.note.restart_changes: The snow line and the winter and summer temperatures apply after the server restarts.
almanac.note.keys: Open this screen from Mod Menu, or bind a key under Options, Controls, Key Binds, Almanac. The key is unbound to start with.
almanac.note.vanilla_players: Players without Almanac get the seasonal weather and colours too, in twelve steps a year, from seasonal copies of each biome. Operators without it can change every setting with /almanac config.
almanac.note.credits: Almanac is new code under the MIT licence. Idea by Fabric Seasons (lucaargolo): biome edits in memory, tracking weather-placed snow. Idea by Serene Seasons (Glitchfiend): sub-seasons and rain timing. Idea by Immersive Snow Reloaded (Straywave and contributors): snow recalculation on chunk load. No code is copied from any of them.
almanac.setting.days_per_season.descript: How many in-game days each season lasts. Each season has an early, mid and late part, so the default 24 gives 8 days to each. The current sub-season and how far into it are kept when this changes. Drag the slider or type an exact number from 3 to 1200 in the box.
almanac.setting.start_sub_season.descrip: The sub-season a world's first day falls in. Changing it doesn't move a world that has already started; use /season set for that.
almanac.setting.paused.description: Stop the calendar. The days still pass, but the season stays where it is until this is switched off.
almanac.setting.announce_sub_seasons.des: Show "Mid Winter has begun" and the like above the hotbar when a sub-season begins.
almanac.setting.snow_line_above_sea: Snow line in cold biomes' early and late summer
almanac.setting.snow_line_above_sea.desc: In early and late summer, cold biomes get rain below this many blocks above sea level and snow above it. Applies after a restart.
almanac.setting.winter_temperature.descr: The temperature given to warmer biomes when winter brings them snow. Vanilla snows below 0.15. Applies after a restart.
almanac.setting.summer_temperature.descr: The temperature given to cold biomes when summer brings them rain. Higher values raise the height at which rain turns to snow. Applies after a restart.
almanac.setting.native_snow_melts_in_sum: Snow that came with a snowy biome melts when summer makes it warm there, and comes back in fall. Only single layers on natural ground melt; snow players place, snow blocks and native ice never do.
almanac.setting.thaw_days.description: How long the season's snow and ice take to melt in loaded chunks when it turns warm, in in-game days. The snow goes in patches that start small and spread. A thaw never takes more than half the sub-season, so short seasons still thaw in time.
almanac.setting.snow_catch_up: Bring loading chunks up to date
almanac.setting.snow_catch_up.descriptio: Chunks that load behind the season (new, or unloaded while it changed) get the season's snow, or lose it, the moment they load. In early spring they keep their snow and thaw like loaded chunks. Off, they always change gradually like loaded chunks.
almanac.setting.catch_up_chunks_per_tick: Chunks brought up to date per tick
At most this many loading chunks are brought up to date each tick; the rest wait for the next tick.
almanac.setting.snow_columns_per_tick.de: How many columns of loaded chunks move one layer of snow towards the season each tick. Higher is faster and costs more.
almanac.setting.vanilla_client_copies: Seasonal biomes for players without Almanac
almanac.setting.vanilla_client_copies.de: Send players without Almanac seasonal copies of each biome, so they see the seasonal weather and colours. Off, they see the real biomes and no seasons at all.
After a sub-season change, players without Almanac get their chunks' biomes again, this many chunks per tick each.
almanac.setting.far_climate_map.descript: Sends players who have Almanac a coarse map of the biomes around them, worked out from the world generator without loading any chunks, so far terrain can show the season's snow. Off, their clients drop the map and far terrain stays as it was drawn.
almanac.setting.far_climate_radius.descr: How far the climate map reaches around each player. Match it to the far terrain's render distance; further costs more sampling on the server and more data for each player.
almanac.setting.far_climate_cell_size.de: The map has one biome per cell. Smaller cells follow biome borders more closely; each halving costs four times the sampling and about three times the data.
almanac.setting.far_climate_bytes_per_ti: At most this much of the climate map goes to each player every tick, nearest first, so joining or travelling never floods a connection.
almanac.setting.colour_blending.descript: Grass and leaves change a little every day. Off, they change once per sub-season, as players without Almanac see them.
almanac.setting.redraw_sections_per_tick: After a colour change, the loaded sections with grass or leaves are redrawn this many per tick, nearest first. Lower is smoother on slower computers; higher finishes sooner.
